Subject: ACME POC: Integration & Success Criteria - Next Steps

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the POC kickoff: 

Recap (from our call)
- Goal: Validate Redwood inference integration for ACME's in-product assistant (scoped to search summarization + action suggestions).
- Primary constraints: 200ms median token latency target for user-facing flows; streaming responses for partial assistant replies; tool-calling to trigger external workflows; data residency in us-west for trial logs.

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Functional: 95% of sampled end-to-end flows produce usable assistant responses (manual review on 50 prompts).
2) Latency: median token latency <= 200ms in our staging environment under realistic concurrency (50 concurrent sessions).
3) Stability: no SLA-impacting errors during a 72-hour soak (<=1% error rate).
4) Integration: SDK-based streaming + tool-calling demo run by ACME engineering team.

Evaluation plan & timeline
- Week 0 (this week): finalize success criteria and owners.
- Week 1: Redwood provides SDK quickstart, sample integration routes, and a test harness. (See attached acme-poc-eval-plan.pdf and redwood-sdk-quickstart.zip)
- Week 2: ACME implements integration in staging; Redwood assists with two 1:1 pairing sessions.
- Week 3: Run 72-hour soak and sampling eval; retrospective and go/no-go.

Ownership (suggested)
- ACME: Priya (tech lead) to own integration; Jordan to own timelines and success signoff.
- Redwood: Marissa (Sales PM) for project coordination; Dev (Solutions Engineer) for technical pairing.

Immediate asks (can you reply with):
1) Confirm the success criteria above (or propose edits).
2) Confirm owners and whether the proposed Week 1 kickoff (Mon 2026-11-30) works for ACME.
3) Any additional compliance items we should prepare for the trial (e.g., security contacts).

I've attached the evaluation plan and a lightweight SDK quickstart zip to get you running. If that looks good I'll send a calendar invite for a 30-minute kickoff.

Thanks, looking forward to this.

Best,

Hi Jordan / Priya,

Quick technical note and an integration checklist so ACME engineering can hit the ground running. See attached integration-checklist.md (lightweight). Main points below: 

API/SDK notes (summary):
- SDK: we provide a Node + Python SDK. The quickstart zip contains example routes.
- Core route: POST /v1/generate (JSON payload: model, prompt, max_tokens, stream boolean).
- Streaming: we support chunked HTTP streaming (Transfer-Encoding: chunked) and SSE for browser clients; we can also proxy via WebSocket if preferred. For the POC, chunked HTTP + SSE is easiest to integrate.
- Tool calling: use the "tools" array in the generate call; Redwood will emit tool_call events in the stream with a structured JSON payload. Example: {"type":"tool_call","tool":"crm_update","args":{...}}. The SDK exposes a handler registration interface for tool handlers.
- KV/prefix caching: recommended to enable for templates to reduce token cost during soak; config flag in SDK: cache.prefix=true.

Suggested short integration checklist: 
1) Install SDK and run quickstart example. (Owner: ACME eng, Due: Day 1)
2) Implement a simple generate call that uses stream=true and render chunks. (Owner: ACME eng, Due: Day 2)
3) Register a demo tool handler and validate tool_call events. (Owner: ACME eng, Due: Day 3)
4) Pairing session with Redwood SE to exercise streaming + tool calls. (Owner: Redwood/ACME, Scheduled: Day 4)
5) Run 72-hour soak in staging and capture latency/metrics. (Owner: ACME, Due: Week 3)

I'll be available for the pairing session and can share a sample curl and Postman collection in the kickoff.

Dev Patel
